l.i: Iesum, qui à sanctis, aut à se, aut alunde fœlicita-

main_text.l: Non: Etsi enim verbo quidem eo Seruato-
re gloriantur, reipsa tamen abnegant vnicum
Seruatorem Iesum{2}. Necesse est enim aut Ie-
sum non esse perfectum Seruatorem, aut qui
eum Seruatorem vera fide amplectuntur, eos
omnia in ipso possidere, quæ ad salutem requi-
runtur{b}.

l.i: Quare appellatur Christus, hoc est, vnctus?

main_text.l: Quód à Patre ordinatus, & Spiritu sancto
vnctus sit{c} summus Propheta ac Doctor,{d} qui
nobis arcanum consilium & omnem volunta-
tem Patris, de redemptione nostri patefecit{e}:
& summus Pontifex,{f} qui nos vnico sacrificio
sui corporis redemit, ac assidué pro nobis apud
Patrem intercedit{g}: & Rex, qui nos suo verbo
& Spiritu gubernat, & partam nobis salutem
tuetur ac conseruat{h}.
Quód per fidem membrum sumus Iesu Chri-
sti,{i} & vnctionis ipsius particeps{k}, vt & nomen
eius confitear{l}, neque sistam ipsi viuam grati-
tudinis hostiam{m}, & in hac vita contra pecca-
tum & Satanam, libera & bona conscientia
pugnem, & postea æternum cum Christo
regnum in omnes creaturas teneam{n}.

l.i: Quam ob causam Christus vocatur filius
Dei vnigenitus, cum nos quoq; simus filii Dei?

page.notes: The marginal references are set in a small, tightly spaced type. Some letters are close together and a few are doubtful, notably "Ies" in note b (read as Ies for Ief), "Ioel" in note k, and the numbers in notes a and m. Where the letter shapes were uncertain I have transcribed them as printed without correction. The superscript reference letters in the text (b to n) have no matching footnotes visible on this part of the page. The sentence "sumus" in the membrum line is read from a damaged join and is doubtful. The phrase "viuam gratitudinis" has an unclear mark after "viuam" and may read differently.
